# Benchmark preparation

This project-specific skill adapts the installed skill-creator grader's evidence and
assertion-critique method; provenance is in `docs/perpetua/roles.md`.
It follows `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`; read that contract and
`goal/goal.md` before designing cases. Protocol and report: the engine contract in your system instructions.
The existing evaluator verifier supplies the independent readiness checks, in another session.

Write only `benchmark/`: protocol, provenance and coverage records, development cases,
repeatable preparation scripts and the optional preparation evidence index. Keep large
originals in `.session/artifacts/` with hashes and source records. Preserve originals before
conversion. Reuse the prepared read-only sources as described in `docs/perpetua/environment.md`.

`benchmark/preparation.json` pins a sha256 for each evidence file. After rebase the engine
runs `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check` and rejects the session when a pinned
file changed without its hash (session #117 was lost this way). Whenever you change a file
listed there, or add evidence for a milestone, rewrite its `sha256` in the same change and
run that check yourself (exit 0 required; it needs no LabVIEW environment). Each evidence
file must stay under 2 MB. If `git commit` fails for a missing identity, leave the changes
staged and say so; the engine commits accepted changes.

For the assigned part of the protocol:

1. State the question, expected observable behavior and verifiable location in the original
   artifact. Establish expected answers independently of the reader being tested. Record
   the method, evidence and uncertainties; unavailable native evidence stays unavailable.
2. Account for artifact families, versions, dependencies and inaccessible diagrams. Keep
   unsupported or unexecuted cases visible. The first corpus does not redefine the goal.
3. Specify project/family splits, duplicate checks and how evaluation cases and answer keys
   will be withheld from the evaluated agent. The repository and its history are public:
   do not commit withheld cases or keys here, including under `policy/evaluator/`.
   Design an access boundary and request missing capability before claiming isolation.
4. Specify matched no-tool and tool baselines, pinned model/prompt/budget, repeats,
   uncertainty and separate reading-fidelity, answer-correctness and source-grounding checks.
5. Exercise the method with wrong answers, wrong source locations, a constant exporter and
   an unsupported case. Link executed evidence and explicit failures. Independently derived
   expectations must distinguish correct and deliberately wrong outputs.

Inspect actual outputs, rather than relying on the execution report. For each expectation,
cite evidence of the substantive result; correct filenames and valid hashes alone do not
pass. Extract and verify implicit factual, process and quality claims. Flag unverifiable
claims and assertions that would also pass a clearly wrong output, or important outcomes
that no assertion checks. These checks adapt the grader instructions; they do not grant
this author independent approval of their own method.

Completion means the assigned evidence is reproducible, not that the benchmark is ready.
Report which prerequisites remain missing. Request a separate reviewer session for the
preparation evidence and a Policymaker-ordered evaluator change when executable scoring is
needed. Only the evaluator role changes `policy/evaluator/`; its independent verifier must
pass before that change takes effect. Product implementation waits for independent method
review and owner acceptance of the pinned protocol and evidence. Numeric thresholds,
scope changes and the goal gate remain owner decisions.

1: # Ocena początkowa i droga do benchmarku
2: 
3: Stan startowy: **skuteczność narzędzia niezmierzona, benchmark nie istnieje**.
4: Temat setupu przygotowuje ocenę; nie buduje produktu ani docelowego zestawu przypadków.
5: Podstawą są ustalenia [niezależnej weryfikacji](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/10#issuecomment-6225343449)
6: i [dostępu do środowiska](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/2#issuecomment-6248028771).
7: Kompilacja przykładu VI z 2014 w kontenerze NI 2026 Q1 dowodzi dostępu do tego środowiska,
8: nie poprawności czytnika, VI Scripting ani obsługi wszystkich wersji. Dostęp 2024 pozostaje niezweryfikowany.
9: 
10: ## Co rozstrzyga skrypt, a co właściciel
11: 
12: Zachowano dostarczoną bramkę `gate.kind: owner`. Każda zmiana pracy czeka na decyzję
13: właściciela; nie zaakceptowano progów jakości ani samodzielnego kończenia celu.
14: Właściciel ocenia treść dowodów, dopuszcza rozpoczęcie implementacji dopiero po wiarygodnej
15: metodzie weryfikacji, akceptuje progi sukcesu i ewentualną zmianę zakresu. W temacie D
16: zaakceptował zasady sukcesu zapisane w `goal/goal.md`: pełny zakres, osobne pomiary
17: wierności odczytu i odpowiedzi popartych źródłem oraz niezależny benchmark z porównaniem.
18: Progi jakości i wykonywalna bramka celu czekają na wiarygodny benchmark i osobną
19: akceptację właściciela; przyszła bramka wymaga `owner_confirms: true`. Plik
20: `goal/gate.yml` pozostaje nieobecny, więc pętla nie ogłasza samodzielnie sukcesu. Zastąpienie
21: bramki skryptem wymaga jego decyzji oraz niezależnie sprawdzonej metody. Nie jest to
22: ograniczenie celu do wersji lub rodzin obecnych w pierwszych przykładach.
23: 
24: `check` uruchamia `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check` w kandydacie. Sprawdza
25: jedynie poprawność opcjonalnego indeksu dowodów: schemat, lokalne ścieżki, niepuste pliki
26: i SHA256. Brak indeksu jest normalnym stanem początkowym, raportowanym jawnie; błędny
27: istniejący indeks zatrzymuje zmianę. Ten check nie potwierdza treści dokumentów ani jakości.
28: Nie wykonuje kodu wskazanego w dowodach. Testy tego skryptu i silnika nie są benchmarkiem LabVIEW.
29: 
30: Raport porównawczy uruchamia się z **zaakceptowanego drzewa**, podając oba katalogi:
31: 
32: ```sh
33: python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --baseline /accepted --candidate /candidate
34: ```
35: 
36: Obsługiwane są też `BASELINE_DIR` i `CANDIDATE_DIR`. Ostatnia linia to JSON zgodny z
37: kontraktem silnika. Raport zawiera oba stany; błędne dowody kandydata dają `rejected`,
38: pozostałe przypadki `inconclusive`, zawsze `improved: false`. Nawet komplet odnośników
39: nie oznacza gotowości benchmarku. `tool_quality: null`, `benchmark_executed: false` oraz
40: `benchmark_ready: false` pozostają jawne. Raport jest pomocą dla właściciela; przy bramce
41: `owner` silnik nie uruchamia go automatycznie i nie wykorzystuje go do automatycznego przyjęcia.
42: Brak pomiaru pozostaje brakiem pomiaru, także po usunięciu lub wymianie indeksu.
43: 
44: Indeks `benchmark/preparation.json` powstanie podczas pracy pętli. Wzór, nie gotowy benchmark:
45: 
46: ```json
47: {"schema_version":1,"milestones":{"sources":[],"tasks":[],"oracle":[],"split":[],"coverage":[],"baseline":[],"challenges":[]}}
48: ```
49: 
50: Każda lista zawiera wpisy `{"path":"benchmark/protocol.md","sha256":"<64 znaki SHA256>"}`.
51: Dowody muszą być plikami w drzewie, bez symlinków, do 2 MB każdy; duże dane opisuje mały
52: rekord z przypiętym źródłem i hashem. Sekcje i liczba odnośników służą nawigacji, nie punktacji.
53: Check działa tylko dla zmian pracy; ścieżki polityki/audytu/dziennika omijają go zgodnie
54: z silnikiem. Weryfikator sam uruchamia testy każdej zmiany evaluatora.
55: 
56: ## Co musi powstać przed implementacją
57: 
58: Pętla przygotuje następujące dowody, następnie niezależny weryfikator sprawdzi metodę,
59: a właściciel oceni jej wiarygodność przed przyjęciem implementacji. Nie wystarczy utworzyć pliki.
60: 
61: | Obszar | Wymagane ustalenia i dowody |
62: |---|---|
63: | sources | Pochodzenie, licencja, commit i SHA256 oryginałów; zależności, wersja zapisu artefaktu i wersja środowiska odczytu osobno. Zachować oryginał przed konwersją. |
64: | tasks | Zadania o przepływie danych, typach, strukturach, zależnościach, projektach i znaczeniu zmian; ocenialna odpowiedź i wskazanie źródła w oryginale. |
65: | oracle | Odpowiedzi ustalone niezależnie od czytnika: diagramy i właściwości w LabVIEW, kontrolowane wejścia/wyjścia, dokumentacja, raporty różnic i zapis niezależnej kontroli. Sam eksport badanego narzędzia nie jest wzorcem. |
66: | split | Rozdział rozwoju i oceny według całych projektów i rodzin; wykrywanie kopii/wariantów. Nowe własne przypadki ograniczają ryzyko znajomości publicznych przykładów przez model. Klucz i część oceniająca poza dostępem badanego agenta; w publicznym repo nie da się ukryć ich samą ścieżką. Przed pomiarem sprawdzić faktyczną izolację. |
67: | coverage | Inwentaryzacja wszystkich rodzin, wersji, modułów i warunków dostępu; pokrycie jawne, bez usuwania trudnych przypadków z mianownika. Pierwszy zestaw nie redefiniuje celu. |
68: | baseline | Powtarzalne porównanie tych samych zadań bez narzędzia, z obrazami gdy dostępne, oraz z narzędziem; ten sam model, prompt i budżet, przypięte wersje, powtórzenia, koszt i czas. |
69: | challenges | Próby metody na celowo błędnych odpowiedziach, błędnych wskazaniach źródła, stałym/pustym eksporcie i nieobsługiwanym przypadku. Zero wykonanych testów, brak runtime lub klucza nie dają zaliczenia. |
70: 
71: Początkowa inwentaryzacja obejmuje VI (panel i diagram), kontrolki i typedefy, biblioteki,
72: klasy, projekty i build specs, testy, zasoby, zależności, pakiety, skompilowane dystrybucje
73: oraz warianty modułów i targetów; lista pozostaje otwarta. Wyniki mają osobne przekroje
74: według rodziny, wersji zapisu i środowiska. Nieprzebadana wersja ma brak pokrycia.
75: Wariant 2024 wolno wybrać dopiero po przedstawieniu dodatkowego nakładu dla wszystkich
76: wersji i ograniczeń zgodności, zgodnie z celem; ten setup nie wybiera wariantu zapasowego.
77: 
78: Przyszły raport oddzieli wierność odczytu od poprawności odpowiedzi agentów i ich poparcia
79: w źródle. Wskaże liczbę zaplanowanych i rzeczywiście wykonanych przypadków oraz wyniki
80: poprawne, częściowe, nieobsługiwane, brak zależności/licencji/środowiska, chroniony/usunięty
81: diagram i błąd narzędzia. Uczciwe zgłoszenie ograniczenia nie dowodzi pełnego odczytu.
82: Sprawdzenie struktury bez sprzętu nie potwierdza zachowania na sprzęcie. Tolerancje,
83: niedeterminizm i przedziały niepewności trzeba określić przed porównaniem. Nie agregować
84: tych wymiarów do arbitralnego jednego wyniku ani nie przyjmować progu sukcesu bez właściciela.
85: 
86: ## Niezależna kontrola zmian
87: 
88: Evaluator zmienia tylko uprawniona rola, na zlecenie Policymakera. Silnik wymaga odrębnej
89: sesji weryfikatora i przypina jej zgodę do commita i drzewa evaluatora. Stara wersja

94: Niezależność oznacza osobną sesję i dowody, nie gwarancję bezbłędności modelu; przy

FILE benchmark/protocol.md
1: # Benchmark method draft
2: 
3: Unpinned, unreviewed design for issue #141; no tasks, keys, split, runs or challenge results are established by this document. No benchmark readiness or product quality is claimed.
4: Authority: [evaluation contract](../docs/perpetua/evaluation.md), [goal](../goal/goal.md), [accepted limits](../docs/perpetua/accepted-limits.md). Current evidence: [sources](sources.md) and [coverage](coverage.md); native semantic inspection of that inventory has not run.
5: Public sources are development material, including their copies and variants. Missing families and versions remain gaps in the full goal; the 2024 fallback is not selected.
6: 
7: ## tasks
8: 
9: Method: create a case specification before testing any reader: question, original artifact identity, family/save version, required dependencies/environment, expected observable, oracle procedure, source locator and explicit uncertainty. Start with public development cases; create withheld cases only inside an approved restricted boundary.
10: Each case asks for concrete claims whose correctness and source grounding can be checked individually. A statement about execution must identify its inputs, state, target and conditions; structural evidence alone cannot establish hardware behavior.
11: 
12: | Family / task | Question and observable to establish independently | Original source to cite |
13: |---|---|---|
14: | VI and VIM | Explain computation, types, structures, dataflow and execution dependencies for controlled inputs; distinguish wired order from scheduling assumptions and specialization. | Panel terminals, diagram nodes/wires, structure/case paths and connector pane; VIM call-site specialization. |
15: | CTL, typedefs and custom controls | Identify type/defaults, strictness and consumers; predict which consumers change or break after a controlled typedef edit. | Control/type properties and original consumer terminals; before/after native observations on derived copies. |
16: | Classes and libraries | Explain membership, scope, inheritance, dispatch and dependency resolution. | LVCLASS/LVLIB item/property paths plus relevant method VI diagrams and native properties. |
17: | Projects and build specifications | Find declared and resolved dependencies, missing items, target settings and build inclusion/exclusion; separate declarations from successful resolution/build. | LVPROJ XML item/property paths and native project/build property views; dependent original files. |
18: | Diagram changes | Explain semantic effects of a controlled pair: behavior-changing edits, presentation-only edits and uncertain effects. | Both original revision hashes and corresponding nodes/wires/cases; native comparison and controlled I/O evidence. |
19: | Menus and resources | Explain menu hierarchy, tags, actions and resource references, including missing resources. | MNU item hierarchy/native properties and referring VI event/handling locations; original resource entries. |
20: | Aliases, project state and configuration | Identify alias mappings and relevant configuration/analysis settings; establish whether a setting is runtime, editor or machine-specific before claiming an effect. | ALIASES, LVLPS and VIANCFG original keys/XML paths plus native interpretation where necessary. |
21: | Packages and archives | Explain dependency constraints, installation contents and contained artifact relationships; identify unresolved or nested members. | VIP/VIPB/VIPC/VSIX/ZIP original manifest/member paths and member hashes; native/package-manager evidence for installation claims. |
22: | Packed libraries and compiled distributions | Identify exposed APIs, linkage and execution requirements; state when diagrams are absent and semantic reading is unavailable. | LVLIBP/native exports and original distribution metadata; controlled API calls where executable. |
23: | Missing and future families | Design dedicated cases for templates, globals, LLBs, shared libraries, tests, XControls/XNodes, executables, real-time/FPGA targets and hardware/module resources; classify CTT/GBL/GLB/LSB/LVSC/LVTEST/RTEXE/RTM/UIR/VIT/XCTL/XNODE by native evidence. | Original family-specific objects/properties, test definitions, target/build settings and observable behavior; unknown formats remain unresolved. |
24: 
25: Archive members inherit their semantic family tasks as well as container/linkage tasks; archive counts do not demonstrate readability. Extension/magic inventory is not an exhaustive family definition.
26: Gradeable answer record: `case_id`, `status`, `claims[{claim_id, answer, conditions, citations[]}]`, `limitations`. Citations contain original SHA256, repository-relative path, archive/member chain when applicable, and a native object/property locator or exact XML/key/byte location appropriate to the claim.
27: For diagrams, record owning VI, nested structure/case, object/terminal/wire identity and native view region; attach a hashed native capture and object map when identifiers are unstable. A screenshot or exported node ID alone is insufficient: the reviewer must resolve the claim back into the preserved original.
28: Before reader exposure, freeze an independently checked reference inventory per task: stable required-claim IDs, atomic facts/relations, conditions, acceptable alternatives, numerical tolerances, original/native reference locators and hashes, and disallowed inferences. Identify separately the required answer claims and required reader observations; neither inventory may be inferred from submitted answers or exports. Record inventory/key revisions and unresolved references. Development keys may be public; withheld keys, case details and revealing evidence must never enter this repository or its history.
29: Account for every required ID and every submitted factual assertion, including implicit assertions in prose and limitations. Preserve the submitted text and its mapping to reference IDs; split compound assertions into atomic claims under frozen rules. Repeated equivalent assertions earn credit once; omissions retain their required slots. An assertion and its negation are a contradiction even when one matches the key: mark the affected item incorrect and retain both assertions. Unmatched assertions enter a separate extra-claim ledger and require independent checking; true extras cannot replace omissions, and false or unverified extras cannot disappear from scoring. Freeze these mapping/adjudication rules before runs and retain scorer/checker decisions.
30: Score reading fidelity, answer correctness and source grounding separately using the following item rules; faithful extraction alone does not establish correct reasoning, and answer correctness cannot establish fidelity.
31: 
32: | Dimension | Required unit and correct outcome | Other item outcomes |
33: |---|---|---|
34: | Reading fidelity | Each fixed required reader observation matches its independently checked native reference, including required types, properties and relations under declared tolerances. | Partially represented compound content is partial; a conflicting value/relation is incorrect; absent content is missing. Unsupported access, inaccessible diagrams, tool errors and unverified native references retain their explicit outcomes and never earn correct credit. |
35: | Answer correctness | Each required answer claim matches an independently established expected claim under its conditions and tolerances. | Incomplete content is partial; false claims or contradictions are incorrect; omitted claims are missing; claims without sufficient independent evidence are unverified. An unsupported-case declaration remains unsupported, not correct. |
36: | Source grounding | Each required answer claim has resolvable original-artifact citations supporting its complete asserted content and conditions. | Support for only part is partial; a wrong or non-supporting citation is incorrect; absent claims/citations are missing; inaccessible evidence is unverified. A correct answer with a wrong citation is incorrect in grounding independently of correctness. |
37: 
38: Reader-observation contract: before exposure, an independent preparer freezes probe IDs, artifact/member hashes, reader entry points and arguments, observation scope, required observation IDs and native-reference alignment rules. Choose probes from the task/native inventories, independently of agent answers and reader outputs; include the types, objects, wires, properties and relationships needed by the task. Pin ordering, limits, any adaptive branches and their selection rules; record unprobed scope as missing coverage. No favorable agent-selected calls may substitute for required probes.
39: For every probe, preserve the exact request, reader/configuration revision, environment, raw response bytes or files and hashes, timestamps, exit/error records and any truncation. Preserve empty responses and failed calls. A separate alignment record maps raw-output locations to required native-reference IDs and records absent, extra, duplicate and contradictory assertions; normalization must retain raw evidence and cannot invent missing facts. Unsupported operations, missing dependencies/licenses/environment, protected/removed diagrams, empty or truncated required content, errors and unverified references never count as matching observations. A successful call or valid wrapper alone earns no fidelity credit.
40: Freeze denominators per task and dimension: all required answer IDs for correctness and grounding, and all required observation IDs for fidelity. Report counts in every item-outcome category over those fixed totals, plus separate extra-claim counts by outcome and contradiction/duplicate counts; do not enlarge denominators with submitted claims or remove unavailable items. Report all planned cases as the coverage denominator alongside attempted/executed/scored counts. Any conditional summary must also show its eligible denominator and excluded/unavailable counts; no single aggregate merges the three dimensions.
41: Apply the following case-assessment rules in order, separately for each dimension. An absent or empty required reference inventory is unverified, never vacuously correct. With an established inventory, any incorrect required item or extra assertion, including a false assertion, contradiction or non-supporting citation in grounding, makes that dimension incorrect. Otherwise, any unverified required item or extra makes it unverified. Otherwise, every required item and extra must be correct (fully supported for grounding) for a correct assessment. Of the remaining cases, any correct/partial required item or extra makes the assessment partial; otherwise any tool error makes it error; otherwise all required items unsupported makes it unsupported; all other combinations of missing/unsupported items make it missing. Keep operational limitations and their affected IDs alongside this assessment; partial, missing, unsupported, unverified and error outcomes never become full passes. These are accounting rules, not owner quality thresholds.
42: Report planned and executed counts and separate dimension-level outcomes, retaining missing dependency/license/environment, protected/removed diagram and tool-error records. Preserve gaps by family, save version, native reading version and target/module; no unavailable case becomes a full-read pass.
43: Deliverable: reviewed development case specifications and a restricted case-schema equivalent, with provenance and coverage mapping. Missing now: native semantic observations, independently checked answers and dedicated cases for uncovered families/versions.
44: 
45: ## oracle
46: 
47: Establish and freeze expected claims before exposing the case to the evaluated reader. The reader's export, reconstructed diagram or answer is never an answer key or the sole evidence for a claim.
48: Preserve and hash original bytes before conversion. Trusted preparation jobs operate on separately hashed working copies; record original save-version evidence separately from native LabVIEW version/build, OS, target, installed modules, licenses and dependency resolution. A successful load in one environment does not establish compatibility elsewhere.
49: Request bounded native cloud jobs with declared artifact hashes, permitted operations, required LabVIEW versions and staged output schemas. Roles receive results, not Docker daemon access. Existing NI 2026 Q1 readiness is environment evidence only; inventory inspection, VI Scripting, other versions and especially native 2024 need their own readiness checks.
50: 
51: | Claim type | Independent establishment procedure | Evidence required for the key |
52: |---|---|---|
53: | Structure, types and properties | Inspect preserved originals in native LabVIEW; use native properties/diagrams and a reviewer-readable capture/object map. Compare text declarations directly with original XML/configuration where applicable. | Original hash and resolvable locator, native property values/captures, inspection method and any inaccessible object. |
54: | Computation and execution dependencies | Choose controlled inputs and initial state; record outputs, errors and relevant execution observations. Inspect dataflow/structures to explain dependencies; one observed schedule cannot prove an ordering guarantee. | Input/output vectors, reset procedure, actual run logs, relevant diagrams and version-specific documentation for semantics. |
55: | Typedef and diagram changes | Preserve both original revisions; apply a documented edit to derived copies, inspect affected consumers/native differences and run discriminating controlled inputs. | Before/after hashes, edit recipe, affected/unaffected checks, native difference evidence and observed behavior. |
56: | Projects, packages and builds | Inspect native project/package properties and original declarations; explicitly check resolution and, where authorized, installation/build behavior in an isolated job. | Declared versus resolved dependency lists, member identities, build settings/results and unresolved items. |
57: | Targets, hardware and compiled artifacts | Inspect available native interfaces and run only with the required runtime, target and hardware or declared simulator. | Actual execution environment and observed scope; simulation or structural inspection cannot certify hardware behavior or recover removed diagrams. |
58: 
59: Documentation supports semantic interpretation only when pinned by version, section/location and content hash or preserved permitted excerpt; it does not establish what a particular original diagram contains. Unavailable documentation remains a gap.
60: An independent checker must resolve each expected claim and citation against original/native evidence without using the reader's output to derive the answer. Record case/key revision, evidence hashes, checker identity/role and session, procedure, claim-level agreement/disagreement and unresolved uncertainty. Disagreement blocks that claim's use as an established key until adjudicated and rechecked.
61: Use more than one observable when necessary to distinguish plausible wrong answers: selected inputs must separate intended computation from known alternatives, and native structural evidence must support dependencies not distinguishable by outputs alone. Record any underdetermined behavior explicitly.
62: Predeclare numeric precision, units, comparison rules, nondeterministic behavior and allowed variation per case.
